fixes.what: Blocking: the La Marche loss is dated 1362, and the 1333 and 1352 keyframes are marked ok with La Marche in them. By the pages the author opened, La Marche left the ducal line in 1341, when Louis I's younger son James took it. Nothing changed hands in 1362: the county passed from James I to his son within the same cadet line.
fixes.why: County of La Marche list: 'Louis I of Bourbon (1322-1341)', then 'James I of Bourbon (1341-1362)'. Duke of Bourbon table: Peter I is duke 1341-1356. House of Bourbon page: 'The remaining line of Bourbons henceforth descended from James I, Count of La Marche, the younger son of Louis I, Duke of Bourbon.' The ledger note says 'The page gives no kinship between the dukes and the La Marche line', but the House page gives it. The K2 note itself says La Marche went to James I, 'not to the dukes Peter I and Louis II'.
fixes.fix: Move the loss to 1341. Use counterpart county-of-la-marche, or 'James I of Bourbon, Count of La Marche'. Change the 1333 keyframe to adjust: the Cliopatria 1333 shape, held 1333-1341 only. Add a new keyframe for 1342-1351 and change the 1352 keyframe to adjust. Both take the Cliopatria 1363 shape (the Bourbonnais alone). Rewrite the K2, K3 and ledger notes.

If the rule is the whole house: keep 1477, but then La Marche stays until the Armagnac marriage (1435/1438) and the 1362 loss is dropped.
